raw_response:
I am old now, and I only started managing the land myself recently, so I do not talk like the extension people. I mostly look at what the neighbors do and keep things steady. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safe way here and we need stable grain income. But I will still keep some cotton, because cotton can bring cash if the price is decent. My family only has 2 people, so I cannot spread myself too thin, and cotton takes more hand work. That is why I will put about 6.1 mu into wheat-maize and 4.0 mu into cotton.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, same as most people here. I will not push fertilizer too hard because cash is tight, but I also do not want the crop to look weak, so I will use a moderate amount, with one base dressing and one topdressing around jointing. If the winter and spring stay dry, I will give 3 irrigations from the well, but not more unless the crop really needs it because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize right away on the same land. The turnaround is short, so I will do simple rotary tillage and sow quickly. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller because it needs more watching and more labor for pest control and picking. I will still use some fertilizer and 2 irrigations if the weather is dry, but I will not spend too much up front.
